questions.prompt: Which factor is NOT an intrinsic factor that controls microbial growth in food?
questions.explanation: Intrinsic factors are properties of the food itself, such as pH, water activity and nutrients. Storage temperature is an extrinsic factor.

questions.prompt: Water activity (aw) of pure water is
questions.explanation: Water activity is the ratio of vapour pressure of the food to that of pure water. Most bacteria need aw above about 0.91.

questions.prompt: Most spoilage bacteria are inhibited when the water activity falls below about
questions.explanation: Lowering aw by drying, salting or adding sugar is the basis of preservation. Xerophilic moulds and osmophilic yeasts grow at lower aw.

questions.prompt: A food with pH below 4.6 is described as
questions.explanation: Low acid foods have pH above 4.6 and require sterilisation to destroy Clostridium botulinum spores in canning.

questions.prompt: Canned low-acid foods are given a severe heat treatment mainly to destroy
questions.explanation: The botulinum cook ensures a 12-log reduction of C. botulinum spores. The anaerobic sealed can would otherwise allow toxin production.

questions.prompt: Staphylococcal food poisoning is caused by

options.text: infection of the gut by live bacteria that take days to grow
a heat-stable enterotoxin made in the food

questions.explanation: The toxin is preformed, so symptoms of vomiting appear within 1 to 6 hours of eating. Cooking later does not destroy the toxin.

questions.prompt: The usual source of staphylococcal food poisoning is

options.text: a food handler with infected skin lesions or nasal carriage

questions.explanation: Staphylococcus aureus grows in cooked food left at room temperature, such as meat, cream and rice dishes.

questions.prompt: Which organism causes a food poisoning with a short incubation of 1 to 6 hours and vomiting in fried rice left at room temperature?
questions.explanation: The emetic form is caused by a heat-stable toxin formed by spores that survive cooking.

questions.prompt: The main cause of gastroenteritis from raw poultry and eggs is
questions.explanation: Salmonella enters the food chain from the gut of birds. Thorough cooking and avoiding cross-contamination reduce risk.

questions.prompt: Botulism is associated with
questions.explanation: Spores germinate in anaerobic, low-acid conditions and produce a heat-labile neurotoxin. Heating food for 10 minutes at 100 degrees C destroys the toxin.

questions.prompt: Listeria monocytogenes is a concern in food because it
questions.explanation: It causes listeriosis, which is dangerous to pregnant women and newborns. Cold storage does not stop it.

questions.prompt: The bacterium that makes lactic acid in fermented milk and gari is
questions.explanation: Lactic acid lowers pH and preserves the food. Cassava fermentation also involves Lactobacillus and Leuconostoc.

questions.prompt: In the production of gari, cassava is fermented to

options.text: reduce cyanide content and develop flavour

questions.explanation: Linamarase from the roots and microbes release hydrogen cyanide, which is lost in drying and roasting.

questions.prompt: The bacteria used in the production of vinegar convert ethanol to acetic acid and belong to the genus
questions.explanation: Acetobacter oxidises ethanol in the presence of oxygen. Yeast first makes the ethanol.

questions.prompt: Pasteurisation of milk is designed mainly to kill

options.text: non-spore-forming pathogens such as Mycobacterium bovis and Brucella

questions.explanation: It is not sterilisation. Pasteurised milk still contains some bacteria, so it needs refrigeration.

questions.prompt: Which test is used to check that milk has been properly pasteurised?

options.text: Methylene blue test only for fat

questions.explanation: Alkaline phosphatase in raw milk is destroyed by pasteurisation, so a positive test means under-heating.

questions.prompt: The methylene blue reduction test is used to judge
questions.explanation: Active microbes use up oxygen and reduce the blue dye to colourless. The faster the decolourisation, the poorer the milk.

questions.prompt: Salting and sugar curing preserve food by
questions.explanation: Osmotic withdrawal of water from microbial cells stops growth.

questions.prompt: Freezing food at minus 18 degrees C

options.text: stops microbial growth but does not kill all microbes

questions.explanation: Frozen food can still carry live organisms that grow again on thawing.

questions.prompt: Irradiation of foods is a method of preservation that

options.text: heats the food to 121 degrees C
uses gamma rays or electron beams to kill microbes

questions.explanation: It reduces spoilage and pathogens without much heat.

questions.prompt: The most common cause of spoilage of bread is

options.text: moulds such as Rhizopus and Aspergillus

questions.explanation: Bread has high carbohydrate and moderate water activity, which favours moulds.

questions.prompt: Souring of milk is due to

options.text: lactic acid formed from lactose by bacteria

questions.explanation: Lactic acid bacteria ferment lactose to lactic acid. The fall in pH causes the casein to curdle.

questions.prompt: Which organism is a mould used in making soy sauce and miso?
questions.explanation: Aspergillus oryzae supplies enzymes that break down soy and wheat.

questions.prompt: Cross-contamination in a kitchen is best prevented by

options.text: storing raw meat above cooked food
using separate chopping boards for raw meat and ready-to-eat food

questions.explanation: Raw foods carry pathogens that can be transferred to food that will not be cooked again.

questions.prompt: The temperature range in which food bacteria grow fastest, called the danger zone, is about
questions.explanation: Food should not stay in this range for more than about two hours.

questions.prompt: HACCP in the food industry stands for

options.text: Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points
High Acidity and Controlled Cooking Procedure

questions.explanation: It identifies hazards, sets critical limits and monitors control points. It is a preventive system, not end-product testing alone.

questions.prompt: The coliform count in food and water is used to show
questions.explanation: Coliforms and E. coli are indicators of faecal contamination.

questions.prompt: Staphylococcal enterotoxin is destroyed by normal cooking.
questions.explanation: The enterotoxin is heat stable. Cooking kills the bacteria but not the preformed toxin.

questions.prompt: Lactic acid bacteria can preserve food by lowering the pH.
questions.explanation: Acid inhibits many spoilage and pathogenic organisms.

questions.prompt: Assertion: Canning of low-acid foods requires temperatures above 100 degrees C. Reason: Spores of Clostridium botulinum survive boiling.

options.text: Both the assertion and the reason are true, and the reason is the correct explanation of the assertion
Both the assertion and the reason are true, but the reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion
The assertion is true but the reason is false
The assertion is false but the reason is true
Both the assertion and the reason are false

questions.explanation: Both are true. Pressure cooking reaches about 121 degrees C and destroys the spores.
